title: What It Takes to Move It: Inertia That Changes and Joints That Pull on Each Other

questions.question: A two link arm's shoulder is accelerated with the elbow stretched out and then with it folded flat. Does it take the same torque for the same acceleration?
options: No, but only because of friction
No: folded flat the arm is 4.0 times easier to swing, because the second link's mass is nearer the shoulder
Yes, the shoulder inertia is a constant of the motor
Yes, only the weight changes
questions.explanation: Measured, 1.176 kg m^2 stretched and 0.296 folded. A mass near the axis is easy to swing, and folding the elbow brings it near.

questions.question: Why does the mass matrix depend on the elbow angle but not on the shoulder angle?
options: The shoulder motor is lighter
It was a simplification in the lesson
Turning the whole arm does not change how its parts are arranged, so it cannot change how hard they are to move
The shoulder angle is measured from the vertical
questions.explanation: Inertia depends on the arrangement of the masses about each axis. Only the elbow changes the arrangement.

questions.question: With gains of 60 and 12 the shoulder overshot by 1.9 percent stretched out and not at all folded, settling 0.22 s later. Why?
options: Damping goes as kd over twice the square root of kp times the inertia, so the same gains give a different damping at a different inertia
A simulation error
The payload moved
The gains were different at each pose
questions.explanation: Lightly damped where the arm is heavy and over damped where it is light. The remedy is to schedule the gains or take the inertia out with the inverse dynamics.

questions.question: Why can the velocity terms of a dynamics model not be tested by holding the arm still?
options: They are tested by the weight
They are too small to measure
The arm cannot be held still
They are proportional to velocity and so are zero at rest: a wrong sign or a missing term is invisible to every static test and to a slow move
questions.explanation: Which is why the energy test is there. A free swing keeps its energy only if every term agrees.

questions.question: A free swing with the velocity terms' signs wrong drifted by 26.6 J in a system that started with 10.5 J. What does that show?
options: The model creates energy from nothing, which no real arm does, so conservation of energy catches a sign error that no static test can
Friction is missing
The payload is too heavy
The simulation is unstable
questions.explanation: With no torque and no friction the total must stay constant. The correct model drifted by 1.5e-06 J.

questions.question: Gravity feedforward tracked a fast move to 281.9 mm worst, and adding the inverse dynamics made it 6.1 mm. What remains for the feedback?
options: Nothing; it is not needed
The weight
Only what the model gets wrong, which on a real arm is friction, backlash and the errors in the link masses, so the 6.1 mm is the best case
The trajectory
questions.explanation: The simulation is the arm exactly as modelled. On hardware the feedforward is worth less and the feedback worth more.
